assumptions: database default isolation: read-committed (PostgreSQL semantics, see docs/phase6/POSTGRES-ISOLATION.md)
a database statement is atomic unless it must wait for another transaction; waiting statements resume with their original snapshot
autocommit (root `db`) statements are single-statement transactions at the default isolation level
local computation is not a scheduling point; it is folded into the preceding transition
rows are read in primary-key order for LIMIT 1 (the declared programs and generated SQL both use ORDER BY the primary key)
tasks of different actors never share a transaction, connection or event loop; actors listed with the same process share in-process variables and crash together
a process crash rolls back open transactions and loses local state; committed data and performed external effects remain

sourceVerification.note: Each actor's ORIGINAL application code ran in its own worker process (an authorized harness) against a private, disposable PostgreSQL database; every SQL statement the application sent was held until the coordinator released it in the order of the model's counterexample, and PostgreSQL's answers (rows, row counts, SQLSTATEs, lock waits reported by pg_stat_activity) were recorded. The invariant was evaluated on the rows the run left in the database. This is evidence about this application, this input and this schedule on this PostgreSQL; it is not a claim about production traffic.
